questions.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati was the founder of which of the following reform association?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__The Arya Samaj was established by Dayananda Saraswati in Mumbai on 10 April 1875.__

__
 
• It is a monotheistic Indian Hindu reform movement that promotes values and practices based on the belief of the Vedas.
 
• It was the first Hindu organization to introduce proselytization in Hinduism.
 
• Although never involved in politics, Swami Dayanand Saraswati was the source of inspiration for variety of political leaders during India's struggle for independence.
 
• For example, the call for '*Swarajya*' was used by him, and later taken by Lokmanya Tilak.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was a part of the organisation.
 
• The Indian Constitution adopted the call for abolition of caste system, untouchability, status of women. All of them were first preached by Arya Samaj.
 
• Today it has branches all over the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Brahmo Samaj**

 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was established in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• The conflict between Keshab Chandra Sen and Debendranath Tagore was broadened in 1865 when Tagore allowed the Brahmos conducting services to wear their sacred threads. 
 
• Keshab objected to this decision and withdrew from the Brahmo Samaj along with his followers.
 
• He established the Brahmo Samaj of India on 15th November 1866.
 
• While on the other hand, Tagore grouped themselves in Adi Brahmo Samaj.
 
 

 
• Veda Samaj__

 
 
• Veda Samaj was established by the efforts of Keshab Chandra Sen and K. Sridharalu Naidu in 1864 at Madras.
 
• The Veda Samaj was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj. 
 
• It worked to abolish caste distinctions and promote widow remarriage and women’s education.
 
• Its members believed in one God. 
 
• They condemned the superstitions and rituals of orthodox Hinduism. 
 
 

 
• Prarthana Samaj:

 
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang.
 
• It was an off-shoot of Brahmo Samaj.
 
• It was a reform movement within Hinduism and Justice M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined it in 1870 and infused new strength to it.
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade, also ran the Deccan Education Society.
 
• Several members of the Prarthana Samaj had earlier been active in the Paramhansa Mandali.
 
• This Samaj denounced idolatry, priestly domination, caste rigidities and preferred monotheism.
 
• It also concentrated on social reforms like inter-dining, inter-marriage, widow remarriage and uplift of women and depressed classes.
 
• Apart from Hindu sects, it also drew upon Christianity and Buddhism.
 
• It sought truth in all religions.
 
• Drawing inspiration from the Maratha Bhakti saints of the medieval period, Ranade sought to establish the concept of one compassionate God.
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu was the Telugu reformer who encouraged the Prarthana Samaj in South India.

questions.question: If the ball, delivered by the bowler, not being a Wide, passes the striker without touching his/her bat or person, any runs completed by the batters from that delivery, or a boundary allowance, shall be credited as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Byes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In cricket,
 
 
• **byes** are runs that the batting team can score when the ball passes the batter without hitting their bat or body, and the fielders are unable to gather the ball in time to prevent the batsmen from completing the runs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Some other Cricket Terminologies
 
 
• **The Delivery**:

 
 
• A bowler delivers a ball that is not wide (it is within the acceptable range for the batter to play).
 
 
 
• **The Ball Passes the Batter**:
 
 
• If the ball passes the batter without touching their bat or person (such as their gloves, body, or pad), it is considered "not hit."
 
• This can happen if the batter misses the ball or if it is a legitimate delivery but the batter is not able to make contact.
 
 
 
• **Runs Scored**:
 
 
• If the batter and their partner run between the wickets during this delivery, these runs are counted as **byes**, not leg runs or any other type of runs. The reason for this is that the runs are completed despite the batter not making contact with the ball, which distinguishes byes from other types of runs, such as leg byes (which occur when the ball touches the batter's body).
 
 
 
• **Boundary Allowance**:
 
 
• If the ball crosses the boundary without being touched by any fielder (whether due to the batter missing or the ball being played in a way that no fielder can intercept it), the batsmen would be credited with a boundary (four or six), and this would also be added to the total score as **byes**.

questions.question: Article 39A of the Indian Constitution deals with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free Legal Aid**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A of the Indian Constitution deals with equal justice and free legal aid.**
 
• The **article was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.**
 
• It mandates that the state ensure that the legal system promotes justice equally and provides free legal aid to all citizens.
 
• The article's language uses the word "shall" twice, which indicates that it is mandatory. 
 
• The **Supreme Court has emphasized that the Constitution mandates legal assistance for poor or indigent accused individuals.**
 
• The** principles of Article 39A are in line with the concept of Public Interest Litigation (PIL)**, which can be filed against the state or central government, and municipal authorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Life**

 
 
• Constitutional Provision: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Over time, the judiciary has broadened the meaning to include:
 
• Right to a clean environment.
 
• Right to privacy (Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017).
 
• Right to health, education, livelihood, etc.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Ra**j
 
 
• Constitutional Provision: Inserted by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992, under Part IX of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom**
 
 
• Constitutional Provision: Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a p block element of the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Magnesium**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Magnesium **is not a p-block element of the periodic table.**
 
• The **p-block elements are groups 13–18 of the periodic table, with the exception of helium.**
 
• Magnesium **is an s-block element, as it belongs to group 2. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phosphorus:**

 
 
• A non-metal that is essential for life and is a key component of DNA, RNA, ATP, and cell membranes
 
 
 
• **Iodine**
 
 
• It belongs to the **halogen group (Group 17)** of the periodic table, which includes other non-metals like fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and astatine. 
 
 
 
• **Silicon**
 
 
• It is classified as a **metalloid**.
 
• Metalloids are elements that have properties intermediate between metals and non-metals.
 
• Silicon is a perfect example of this category.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Here are some other elements and their blocks:
 
• **Germanium:**
 
 
• A p-block element that is a lustrous, hard, greyish-white metalloid 
 
 
 
• **Manganese:**
 
 
• A d-block element that is often found in minerals in combination with iron 
 
 
 
• **Technetium: **
 
 
• **​**A d-block element that is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive 
 
 
 
• **Rhenium: **
 
 
• **​**A d-block element that is a silvery-white, heavy, third-row transition metal 
 
 
 
• **Halogens:**
 
 
• A group of five elements (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, and astatine) that are p-block elements

questions.question: The actor's performance in a ___________ plays is completely speechless, the story is enacted using a vocabulary of facial expressions and hand-gestures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **actor's performance in a Kathakali plays is completely speechless** the 'libretto' is sung by two singers on the stage who keep time on gong and cymbals, while a pair of drummers also on the stage play the Chenda.
 
• It is characterized by:
 
 
• **Speechless performance:** The story is enacted without spoken words.
 
• **Facial expressions and hand gestures:** A rich vocabulary of **mudras** (hand gestures) and **abhinaya** (facial expressions) are used to convey the narrative.
 
• **Elaborate costumes and makeup:** These enhance the visual storytelling.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Odissi Dance**
 
 
• Originates from **Odisha and is one of the oldest classical dance forms.**
 
• **Known for its lyrical movements** and depiction of spiritual themes from the Vaishnavite tradition, particularly about Lord Jagannath and stories from the Gita Govinda.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Dance**
 
 
• Originates from Manipur in northeastern India.
 
• **Known for its soft, graceful movements **and storytelling through expressions and mudras (hand gestures).
 
• Focuses on themes from Vaishnavism, particularly stories of Radha and Krishna.

questions.question: Who among the following received Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to tribal dance Baiga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arjun Singh Dhurwey**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** is one of India's most prestigious honors for individuals who have made significant contributions to the performing arts, including music, dance, drama, folk arts, and traditional forms.
 
• **Arjun Singh Dhurwey** is a prominent exponent of **Baiga dance**, a traditional tribal dance form performed by the **Baiga tribe** of Central India, particularly in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• Baiga dance is deeply rooted in the tribal community's cultural and religious traditions. It is performed during festivals, rituals, and community celebrations, showcasing their connection to nature and spirituality.
 
• Arjun Singh Dhurwey has been instrumental in preserving and popularizing this tribal dance form, which is an integral part of India's rich intangible cultural heritage.
 
• His dedication to keeping the tradition alive and his contribution to the broader recognition of tribal art forms earned him the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hem Chandra Goswami** is known for his contributions to Sattriya dance.
 
• **Tankeswar Hazarika Borbayan** is recognized for his work in Sattriya dance as well.
 
• **Som Datt Battu** is known for his contributions to folk music, not tribal dance.

questions.question: The National Savings (Monthly Income Account) Scheme, 2019 has been amended through ___________.

• The account matures in five years
 
• The minimum deposit is ₹1,000, and the maximum is ₹900,000 for a single account and ₹1,500,000 for a joint account
 
• A depositor can open more than one account under the scheme
 
• A guardian can open an account for a minor or a person of unsound mind
 
• An account can be closed prematurely after one year, but before three years, with a deduction of 2% of the deposit
 
• If an account is closed after three years, 1% of the deposit will be deducted
